post.description: Pairs this browser with a code from a trusted client, and sets its token cookie.

Pairs a client that keeps its own token (a browser extension, whose requests carry no
cookie of the browser's) with a code from a trusted client, and gives it the token.
Unpairs the calling device.
A one-time code for pairing another device.

get.description:
Everything that changes while no run is open: memory, skills, jobs, integrations, runs
started from other channels. Clients keep this open for their whole session, so it also
tells which clients are connected. A new connection starts from now; a reconnection sends
the last id it received and gets what it missed.

post.description:
Moves the calling client to the inbox, which routes each message to its conversation, leaving the
one it was on.
A new conversation for the calling client, which leaves the one it was on.
The calling client closes its conversation without moving to another, as a closed chat tab.

put.description: Replaces one profile section with the user's own list. 422: an unknown section or too many items.

post.description: Sends a message the inbox sent on (a Dispatched event) here, as it was written.

Asks in the inbox where a message it sent on goes instead, and sends it on again (a Dispatched
event).

get.description:
Replies in progress in any conversation, oldest first. `run` and `run_finished` events tell
when this changes.

schema.title: Response Runs In Progress Runs Get

get.description:
Its messages up to its runs in progress, and those runs, oldest first, which a client follows from
their start (`/runs/<id>/events`) to show them as if it had been watching.

One conversation as the list shows it: its title, tags and channels. 404: it isn't listed (a new one
before its first message); `conversations` events tell when it changes.

delete.description:
Deletes a conversation no client is on. 404: no such conversation; 409: a client is on
it or a reply is running.

schema.title: Response Conversation Messages Conversations  Thread Id  Messages Get

get.description:
A tool call in full: its messages show each call's arguments on one line and the start of its output,
`partial` when that leaves something out. 404: the conversation has no such call.

A step inside a tool call in full (a delegate call's subagent's, a task's, a handed-off agent's own
subagent's), by its place from 0: the call shows each step's start, `partial` when that leaves something
out. 404: the call has no such step.

Its messages, tokens and tool calls, and when it started and was last written in. All zero for a
new one; `run_finished` events tell when they may have changed.

What its run stopped to ask and still waits for, whoever started it, so a client opening it
can ask the user. Answered with POST /threads/<id>/approvals; empty when nothing waits.

schema.title: Response Pending Approvals Conversations  Thread Id  Approvals Get

post.description: Moves the calling client to an earlier conversation, leaving the one it was on.

schema.title: Response Saved Facts Memory Facts Get
Response Saved Episodes Memory Episodes Get

get.description: The agents installed plugins bring, with the command the apps offer for each.
The folders the apps offer to hand a conversation to: the workspace and the ones used before.

The folders inside `path`, to browse to one; hidden ones (named with a dot) too when `hidden`. 400: not
a full path, or it can't be read.

put.description: 400: no plugin brings that agent, or the folder doesn't exist.

post.description:
Passes a message, and the files sent with it, on to the agent while it works on the conversation's
last one; it takes it between its steps. 400: neither text nor files. 409: it isn't working, or can't
take messages while it works.
Stops the agent's step in progress; it waits for the next message. 409 as for messages.

get.description:
The files in the user's conversations, sent by them or brought by tool results, newest first: those
matching `q` (name, type, where it came from or conversation), from `offset`, at most `limit` (all
without it).
One of those files, by its path in the list, to view or save. 404: no such file.

post.description: 409: the channel isn't connected.

get.description:
The channel's limits come with the request: how often it may edit a message, how long a
draft and a message may be, and whether it sends voice notes.

post.description:
`voice`: the message was a voice note (Settings → Audio can speak only those replies). `reply_to`:
the id of the message it replies to, whose conversation it goes on in; `message`: its own id.

get.description: The presets of the email plugins that are on.

schema.title: Response Email Providers Integrations Email Providers Get

get.description: The default account first.

schema.title: Response Email Accounts Integrations Email Accounts Get

post.description: Checks the logins with the servers first. The first account becomes the default.

The provider's sign-in page; the browser comes back to `redirect_uri`. 400: unknown
provider or missing values. 404: unknown account.

put.description: Only the name; the sign-in stays.

get.description: Who the agent may email without asking, from any account, besides the user's own accounts.

post.description:
The last step of a sign-in (an email account, a remote MCP server). Open to unpaired
browsers: the one-time state is the proof (the web app's /app/oauth page may be opened on
the daemon's own computer, before pairing). 400: expired state, refused code, or a server
that won't work with the tokens.

put.description: 404: no such skill. 400: built in, or the text is empty.

delete.description: 404: no such skill. 400: built in, or it comes with an MCP server.

post.description:
Install the skill again from its repository. 404: no such skill. 400: not installed, or
the repository can't be read.

get.description: The reply of the job's run that started `at`, as the notification of that run links to it.

schema.title: Response Mcp Servers Mcp Servers Get

post.description:
Connect once and list the server's tools, without saving it. A remote server may ask to
sign in instead: it can be added, then signed in to.

delete.description:
With `delete_data`, the server's data folder goes too; otherwise it stays. Its keys stay
until the user deletes them (`kept`, POST /plugins/keys/forget).

post.description:
The server's sign-in page; the browser comes back to `redirect_uri`, which finishes it
(/oauth/finish). 404: no such server. 400: a local server, one that can't be reached or
doesn't ask to sign in.

Install the server again from its repository. 404: no such server. 400: not installed
from one, the repository can't be read, or the new version needs a value not given yet.

get.description:
MCP servers and skills that keep failing, and the health check's new or growing causes, the newest
first.

post.description: Checks today so far in the background, unless a check runs; its report comes with a `doctor` event.

put.description: The cause is noise: left out from now on. 404: the latest check didn't find it.

delete.description: The cause shows again from the next check. 404: it wasn't marked.

get.description: The newest first, from `offset`, at most `limit` (all without it).

post.description:
Builds the sections again in the background, unless a refresh runs or, unforced, the last one is
under ten minutes old.

put.description:
The calling client shows Home: it's refreshed every half hour while it does, until DELETE or until the
client disconnects.
The new and changed ones are built in the background. 400: sections that can't be saved.

get.description: Coding agents' tasks still running, the newest first, with their latest steps.

schema.title: Response Running Tasks Agent Tasks Running Get

get.description:
Installed plugins the extras have a newer version of, as of the last check. Empty while
checks are off.

schema.title: Response Plugin Updates Repositories Updates Get

get.description: The repositories plugins are listed from: the official extras first, then the added ones.

post.description: 400: listed already, can't be read (with the token, for a private one), or offers no plugins.
Its installed plugins stay. 400: the extras, or a repository not listed.

get.description:
Everything removed plugins left kept: each plugin's keys while it isn't installed again (`repository`
empty), and each private repository's token nothing needs any more (`plugin` empty). `plugins` and
`settings` events tell when it may have changed.

schema.title: Response Kept Plugin Keys Plugins Keys Get

post.description: Delete what a removed plugin left kept (Removed.kept), when the user says so.

get.description:
What every listed repository offers; one that can't be read has an error instead.
`cached=true` answers from the listings kept from the last read, reaching only a repository
never read; a read that finds something new publishes `plugins`.

schema.title: Response Repository Plugins Repositories Plugins Get

post.description: The skills and MCP servers a git repository offers. 400: it can't be read or has none.
400: the repository can't be read, lacks something picked, a name is taken, or a field is empty.

schema.title: Response Prompt Sections Settings Prompts Get

put.description: 404: not a prompt the user can edit. 400: an empty text, or the edit can't be written.

delete.description: Back to the built-in text. 404: not a prompt the user can edit. 400: the edit can't be deleted.

post.description:
Keeps the edit as it is after the built-in text changed (`built_in_changes`), which isn't said again.
404: not a prompt the user can edit. 400: that can't be recorded.
The text read aloud on this host (Kokoro), as WAV.

schema.title: Response Model Providers Settings Model Providers Get

put.description: Checks that both models answer with these settings, then uses them.

post.description:
The models the provider offers for these values, to pick from; empty when it can't list
them. 400: the provider refused the values or can't be reached.

schema.title: Response Available Models Settings Model Available Post

get.description: Tokens and cost of the model calls, by day, model, purpose, channel, conversation, job, skill and tool.

The computer the daemon runs on: system, versions, CPU, memory, disk, uptime and load, and why the
daemon can't be stopped from the apps now, if it can't.

post.description:
Installs start at boot again, bringing an out-of-date one up to date (`outdated`). A daemon it started
restarts once no run is in progress, which can't be taken back. 400: it's off, or the password was refused.

get.description: The restart or stop waiting for runs to end; `ending` is "" when none is.

delete.description:
The daemon keeps running. 409: nothing is waiting, it already went ahead, or something needs it (an
update installed, start at boot installed again: `can_take_back` is false), so it can't be taken back.

post.description: Cancels the runs the restart or stop waits for, so it goes ahead. 409: nothing is waiting.

get.description: As of the last check; doesn't reach the repository.

post.description:
Starts installing what's new; the daemon restarts once it's installed and no run is in progress. 409:
nothing to install, or it can't be installed here, with why.
Fetches the repository and says what's new.

get.description: The latest `lines` entries at `level` or above from `component`, oldest first. 400: an unknown component.

A `page` event like GET /logs/{name}, then an `entry` event for each new matching entry.
Every connection, a reconnection too, starts with its page.

ApprovalRequired.title: ApprovalRequired
ApprovalRequired.description:
The run waits for the user. Usually an approval, answered with {"approved", "reason"}; a
request whose `kind` is QUESTION is a question with options (core/tools/questions.py), with
`question`, `options` and `multiple`, answered with {"choices": [picked options]}. One whose
`kind` is PLUGIN_OFFER offers a plugin from the extras (core/tools/plugins.py), with `name`,
`description` and the plugin as the repository lists it (`server` or `skill`): the app installs
it through its usual route and answers {"installed": bool}. One whose `kind` is PLUGIN_SETUP
opens an installed plugin's setup (its email accounts, a channel's pairing), with `name`,
`description` and `server`, answered with {"done": true} once the user closes it.

Cause.title: Cause
Cause.description:
One cause and how often it happened in the day. `id` stays the same across days and versions: it's made
of the kind, the text with its numbers and ids left out, and where it happened, without line numbers.

ChannelPress.title: ChannelPress
ChannelPress.description: A button pressed in a chat: the button's data, on `message` whose text is `text`.

Commit.title: Commit
Commit.description: A version of lo9i: a commit of its repository. `date` is the commit's, ISO 8601.

ConnectedClient.title: ConnectedClient
ConnectedClient.description:
A client holding the daemon's event stream open. `transport` is "unix socket" or host:port.
`device_id` is the paired device it connected from (empty on the Unix socket), `thread_id` the
conversation it's on (empty until it starts, resumes or writes to one).

ConversationStats.title: ConversationStats
ConversationStats.description:
`input_tokens` counts the cache reads too. The times are None for a conversation not in the list
(a new one before its first message). The context is the assistant's or, while the conversation is handed
to an agent, that agent's (`context_agent` its name), as of its last answer; 0 when it's not known.

DoctorPage.title: DoctorPage
DoctorPage.description: The latest report, the causes marked as known, and whether a check runs now.

FoundServer.title: FoundServer
FoundServer.description: An MCP server in a repository, before it's installed.

FoundSkill.title: FoundSkill
FoundSkill.description: A skill in a repository, before it's installed.

Handoff.title: Handoff
Handoff.description: The agent a conversation is with, and the folder it works in.

title.title: Title
title.description: What it is, in a few words: the event, the show or movie, the bill.

subtitle.title: Subtitle
subtitle.description: One short line more, or empty: where, which episode, how much.

date.title: Date
date.description: Its day as YYYY-MM-DD, or empty when it has none.

time.title: Time
time.description: Its time of day as HH:MM, 24-hour, or empty when it has none.

HomeItem.title: HomeItem
HomeItem.description: One thing the section shows: an event, an episode, a bill.

HomeSection.title: HomeSection
HomeSection.description: A section as the user wrote it.

HostStatus.title: HostStatus
HostStatus.description:
The computer the daemon runs on. Sizes in bytes, percentages 0-100, `load_average` over 1, 5 and
15 minutes (empty where the system has none).

JobRunReply.title: JobRunReply
JobRunReply.description: A job run's whole reply; its record keeps only the end of it.

KeptKeys.title: KeptKeys
KeptKeys.description:
What a removed plugin left kept, for the user to keep or delete: its keys' names, and the
token of the private repository it came from when nothing else needs that any more.

KnownCause.title: KnownCause
KnownCause.description: Recurring noise that isn't a problem: left out of every report from then on.

LogEntry.title: LogEntry
LogEntry.description:
One record. `message` keeps every line of it. Text before the first record of a file (output
that isn't a record) has no time, level or logger.

LogPage.title: LogPage
LogPage.description: The latest matching entries, oldest first.

McpServerChange.title: McpServerChange
McpServerChange.description: Fields to change; the ones left out keep their value.

McpServerStatus.title: McpServerStatus
McpServerStatus.description: What a client shows. Has the names of env values and headers, never the values.

Me.title: Me
Me.description: The caller: a trusted client (Unix socket), or the paired device it is.

MemorySnapshot.title: MemorySnapshot
MemorySnapshot.description: What the assistant currently knows about the user, in plain types for gateways.

ModelProvider.title: ModelProvider
ModelProvider.description: A provider clients offer, with what it asks for and the models to suggest.

ModelStatus.title: ModelStatus
ModelStatus.description: What a client shows. Says which secret values are set, never the values.

PendingEnding.title: PendingEnding
PendingEnding.description:
The restart or stop waiting for runs to end, and for an update being installed; `ending` is "" when none
is. `can_take_back` is false when something needs it, which `needed_by` says ("An update was installed").

RepositoryPlugins.title: RepositoryPlugins
RepositoryPlugins.description: What one repository offers, or why it couldn't be read.

ServerField.title: ServerField
ServerField.description: A value the user gives when installing: an env value of a local server, a header of a remote one.

SetupItem.title: SetupItem
SetupItem.description:
A line the apps show for a channel: text, a code to read out, a value to copy, a QR code to scan
(`value` is what it encodes; each app draws it) or a button (`value` is the action it sends back).

ShownCall.title: ShownCall
ShownCall.description: A tool call of the assistant's in full, loaded when the user opens it.

ShownConversation.title: ShownConversation
ShownConversation.description: A conversation as a client opens it while its runs may be in progress.

ShownStep.title: ShownStep
ShownStep.description:
A tool call inside a delegate call (its subagent's), a task_status call (the task's) or a handed-off
agent's call (its own subagent's): its arguments and the start of its output, `partial` when they leave
something out, so the whole step is worth loading (`tool_call_step`).

ShutdownStatus.title: ShutdownStatus
ShutdownStatus.description: A requested restart or stop: the daemon restarts or stops once these runs end, at once when none.

SpeechStatus.title: SpeechStatus
SpeechStatus.description: The chosen settings and what can be chosen.

StartingContext.title: StartingContext
StartingContext.description:
The context a new conversation starts with, its system prompt and tool definitions, against the window
the conversation's context is measured against (the chat's context bar).

StartupStatus.title: StartupStatus
StartupStatus.description: Whether the daemon starts at boot, and whether this daemon was started that way.

TokenRow.title: TokenRow
TokenRow.description:
Tokens of one day, model, conversation, tool... `cost` in US dollars, None when no model
involved has a price (core/usage/prices.py).

UpdateStatus.title: UpdateStatus
UpdateStatus.description:
The version the daemon runs and whether a newer one can be installed from the app (daemon/updates.py).

`installed_from`: "git" (a clone the app can update), "deployed" (copied from another computer by
scripts/deploy.sh, updated from there) or "package" (neither, nothing to compare against).
`state`: idle, checking, updating (`step` says what it does), failed (`error` says why) or restarting.
`new`: the commits the update brings, newest first, as of the last check (`checked_at`, ISO 8601).
`reason`: why it can't be updated from the app, when `can_update` is false.

WebSearchStatus.title: WebSearchStatus
WebSearchStatus.description: What a settings screen shows. Never includes the key.
